title: chore(examples): implement e-commerce demo mobile design
body:
## Description

This implements the mobile design of the e-commerce demo. Since the theme we provide is desktop-first, I wrote the demo style desktop-first.

## Preview

[See preview →](https://deploy-preview-3866--instantsearchjs.netlify.com/examples/e-commerce)

## Implementation

I took some decisions on how to develop the mobile adaptation to the e-commerce demo. Let me know if you think that some are not appropriate.

- I used `data-` attributes for multiple purposes.
    - `data-widget="widget-name"` to be explicit on which element is related to an InstantSearch widget (I didn't specified an `id`)
    - `data-layout="mobile|desktop"` to filter out the elements that shouldn't be displayed on mobile or desktop
- SVGs have a `viewbox` attribute so that they can be scaled via CSS
- Once the user refines the filters, it scrolls to the results container
- `position: sticky;` is used for the button at the bottom of the filters panel but is not supported on iOS

## Notes

Here are some notes on things that we can improve.

- The correct breakpoint to trigger to the mobile design is to be defined by Nico
- The animation is not great and I plan to revisit it. I'd appreciate some suggestions on how to make it look better.
- The hit layout overflows on small screens (see page 3)
- I'm not convinced with the chosen CSS naming so I'm in for suggestions

## Related

- [Design](https://app.zeplin.io/project/5acc8becfc0c980068fc12cc/screen/5d03a7333916305e0ad8e492)

Deploy preview for *instantsearchjs* ready!

Built with commit c799028bb1ec15894473b826088337f8888e252c

https://deploy-preview-3866--instantsearchjs.netlify.com

I'm not sure about the two buttons at the bottom. Whatever filters I modify, it's taken into account instantly. It means there's nothing to "save". It's kind of already saved. Intead of "Save and close", it should be just "Close" IMO.
If there should be a "save" button, I think it should work like this:
- Filter A is applied.
- User opens up the filter popup.
- User applies Filter B.
- User doesn't clicks "save" button but "close" button.
- The only filter applied now is still A.

According to current behaviors of our widgets, "reset" and "close" buttons seem to be enough. What do you think?

@eunjae-lee I agree with you. Here is my proposal to Nico, waiting for his approval.

<details>
<summary>Show proposal</summary>

![Filters overlay](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6137112/59851360-c4433280-936c-11e9-81a2-428ad588ef32.gif)

</details>

What do you think?

I think it's better. I also thought about not having the bottom buttons view at all and having a reset button somewhere around "Filters" title and having a simple "X" close button somewhere top-right corner, but haven't got any proper proposal. I'm fine with yours.
Could you explain to me more about why we're using `data-widget="widget-name"` instead of `id`? What do we get from this?

It's mainly to make it clear that a container is used for an InstantSearch widget. With `id` we don't know if it's used for styling, JavaScript interactions, etc.

It's not super important but I'm trying different patterns while building this demo.

Besides, we're becoming a `data-driven` company... haha
haha okay. let's give it a go!

FYI, [here](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3866/files#diff-e8c7e43cd3cdd0ff527be8f88d1d02acR80), `.container-body > div` is changed to `.container-body .ais-Panel` because the root element of `ais-panel` widget is not a `div` in Angular InstantSearch.


plus, [the line 105](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3866/files#diff-e8c7e43cd3cdd0ff527be8f88d1d02acR105) is changed to `.container-options div {` from `.container-options > div:not(:first-of-type) {` for the same reason.
The dynamic save button with the number of hits was approved by Nico so I implemented it.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/499898/59929388-076ed580-9441-11e9-8c77-fa1af00cb029.png)

unwanted gap there.

Not a blocker to me, but I'm interested to learn later how to fix this if anyone already knows.
